content: Paddy requires 1000-1500 mm water throughout growth cycle. Ideal temperature range is 22°C - 32°C. In nursery and tillering stages, maintain 2-3 cm water level. High humidity (>80%) combined with temperatures between 20-28°C triggers fungal blast (Pyricularia oryzae). Avoid excessive urea when blast is spotted; apply Tricyclazole or validamycin. Ensure field bunds are cut to drain excess water during heavy rain alerts.

Cotton requires warm, sunny climate (25°C - 35°C). High rainfall at square formation and boll development causes square shedding and boll rotting. Warm humid weather (RH > 70%, Temp > 28°C) causes rapid outbreak of Whitefly and Pink Bollworm. Spraying must only be performed when wind is below 15 km/h and no rain is expected for 24 hours to prevent pesticide washoff.

Wheat is a cool-season Rabi crop. Optimum temperature for tillering is 16-20°C and for grain filling is 20-23°C. Terminal heat stress (sudden rise in temperature > 30°C during February/March) causes premature forced maturity and shriveled grains. Apply light irrigation or spray 0.2% Potassium Nitrate (KNO3) to mitigate terminal heat shock. Dew and cloudy weather favor Yellow Rust (Puccinia striiformis).

Mustard requires dry and cool weather. Overcast, cloudy weather with persistent morning fog and relative humidity above 75% triggers heavy Mustard Aphid (Lipaphis erysimi) infestation during flowering and pod development. Inspect borders of fields. Spray insecticides in the late afternoon to avoid harming pollinating honeybees.
